To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MUs are recognised by policy makers, industry, and academia, and are considered as joint ventures, which enable the synergy of interests and minimise conflicts.
the multi-use concept is not yet fully developed and implemented in the Eastern Atlantic region, however, it is a promising approach for the future.

multi-use is a concept that is gaining momentum in maritime space, and that it is a promising tool for achieving synergies between different maritime uses, but that it needs a more holistic approach to be fully implemented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the promotion of MUs as joint ventures, which can enable synergies of interests and minimize conflicts, while respecting national maritime planning cultures and existing MUs experience.
the development and application of a novel methodology to assess and compare the potential for MUs in the context of MSP, in the Eastern Atlantic.
the promotion of MUs as a way to increase the efficiency of marine resources and the sustainability of maritime economies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MUs can contribute to sustainable maritime economies and ecosystems, however, the extent and the way in which they do so, is dependent upon the national and local contexts and the specific MU.

the implementation of MUs is a complex process, which is not only related to the technological and economic maturity of the sectors involved, but also to the national and regional planning culture and to the maturity of maritime policy.
MUs are not a panacea, but rather a useful tool to promote co-existence and to minimise conflicts in the maritime space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the EU and its member states need to work on the development of a common approach for the implementation and monitoring of MUs, and that the EU needs to support the development of national strategies and policies, and to promote the development of innovative MUs.
the Eastern Atlantic is a promising region for MUs, however, the potential for their development is still underexploited, and further efforts are needed to realise their benefits.
MUs are a promising tool in MSP and can contribute to the development of the maritime economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Eastern Atlantic sea-basin is a promising area for MU development and that the EU can support this process by providing a framework for multi-sectoral cooperation and by developing a shared vision for the sea-basin.
MUs can contribute to the sustainable development of the maritime economy, and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

MUs are not a new concept in the Eastern Atlantic, and the identified gaps and barriers can be overcome through the engagement of the private sector and the development of innovative solutions, which can be further promoted through the implementation of European strategies and actions.
